1225644_b04389b4.text: The overwhelming majority of these studies have focused on inputs to and projections from the dorsal lateral geniculate nucleus (dLGN). Relay neurons within dLGN receive strong glutamatergic inputs from retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) and serve as the principle conduit of visual signaling to the cortex. However, relay neurons do not act as passive relays of visual information. The gain of retinogeniculate signal transmission is modulated by nonretinal inputs to dLGN. These nonretinal inputs arise from visual cortex, pretectum, brainstem, thalamic reticular nuclei, and local dLGN interneurons, and they far outnumber the more powerful retinal inputs (Sherman et al., 2002)(Sherman, 2004). In fact, nonretinal inputs account for as much as 95% of the nerve terminals in dLGN (Sherman et al., 2002)(Erisir et al., 1997)(Erisir et al., 1997)(Horn et al., 2000)(Bickford et al., 2010)

1225644_a88750af.text: .One set of nerve terminals contain flattened, oval shaped synaptic vesicles, a hallmark feature of inhibitory GABAergic terminals, and are therefore called F terminals (Sherman, 2004)(Lund et al., 1972)(Famiglietti, 1970). In dLGN, GABAergic terminals arise from the thalamic reticular nucleus and local inhibitory interneurons [7,18]19].
